*Broadcom, Chainguard, Echo, IBM/Red Hat, Moderne, TuxCare, and Seal Security partner with JFrog to deliver a unified, policy-driven pipeline for automated vulnerability resolution at agentic speed*
SUNNYVALE, Calif.
& NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- **swampUP 2026 — ** JFrog Ltd.
(Nasdaq: FROG), creators of the JFrog Software Supply Chain Platform, the system of record for trusted software artifacts, binaries, and AI assets, today introduced JFrog Zero-Touch Remediation and announced the initial partners in its JFrog Self-Healing Software Supply Chain Security Ecosystem.
Zero-Touch Remediation automatically finds the best available fix for a known vulnerability from any ecosystem partner and applies it through the customer's pipeline, without breaking a build, forcing a version update, or disrupting developer workflows.
Together, JFrog and its ecosystem partners neutralize vulnerabilities before attackers can exploit them - shrinking the gap between discovery and remediated patch to near-zero – turning the self-healing software supply chain from a concept into a working reality.
...
JFrog Zero-Touch Remediation is available immediately as part of JFrog Unified Security.
Interested customers can schedule a live demonstration here.
To learn more about JFrog Zero-Touch Remediation read this blog or register for the *“* *Secure at Frontier Speed* *,*” webinar on Wednesday, September 30 at 11 AM PT/2 PM ET.

*The leader in software supply chain security collaborates with the leading cloud and AI security platform to deliver a single source of truth from code to cloud to runtime – giving teams the visibility and speed to remediate threats before attackers exploit them*
SUNNYVALE, Calif.
& NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- **swampUP 2026 **— JFrog Ltd (Nasdaq: FROG), creators of the JFrog Software Supply Chain Platform, the system of record for trusted software artifacts, binaries, and AI assets, today announced a new integration with Wiz, now part of Google Cloud, that closes a critical gap in AI-Era security: shrinking the time between risk detection and verified code fixes.
The JFrog Platform serves as the single source of truth for all software artifacts – from build to production – while the Wiz cloud and AI security platform adds instant cloud runtime visibility.
Together, the integration enables security and engineering teams with a unified view of what's running, where it came from, whether it's trusted, and how to fix it – enabling teams to keep pace with frontier AI models that move faster than most organizations can respond.
...
The JFrog-Wiz integration is designed to close this gap by connecting both halves of the picture in real time.
The integration operates through an API-based data workflow.
Wiz identifies vulnerable and exposed workloads across cloud environments and JFrog traces each workload back to its source artifact in JFrog Artifactory, enriches it with JFrog Advanced Security vulnerability findings, Contextual Analysis, and AppTrust provenance data.
Together, security teams get a unified view and full control: what's running, where it came from, whether it's trusted, and how to fix it – without building custom dashboards or manual correlation.
The result: teams spend less time reconstructing context and more time remediating.
The JFrog integration with Wiz delivers:
- **Faster risk-to-fix motion: ** What previously took days of manual investigation now takes hours.
Security teams see Wiz findings and JFrog supply chain context in one unified view on the Wiz Security Graph with no manual correlation required.
...
- **Automatic detection of untrusted deployments: ** Untrusted images running from unapproved registries are flagged automatically.
Remediation paths trace directly to the build pipeline, with fix availability confirmed against existing Artifactory artifacts.
- **Zero-friction integration: ** Based on an API connection, the integration requires no new agents, no cluster instrumentation, and no elevated cloud permissions.
Customers running both JFrog Advanced Security and Wiz can operationalize this integration in just minutes.
...
The JFrog-Wiz integration is available to customers immediately and ships as part of JFrog Advanced Security.
To learn more and see the integration in action visit www.jfrog.com/jfrog-and-wiz.

Source: JFrog Ltd.","source":"web","title":"JFrog Delivers Trust Layer for AI-Driven Software with NVIDIA","url":"https://investors.jfrog.com/news/news-details/2026/JFrog-Delivers-Trust-Layer-for-AI-Driven-Software-with-NVIDIA/default.aspx"}],"type":"search_results"},{"contents":[{"snippet":"1. **August 27, 2026 release: announcement, availability, and significance**

   **Announcement:** JFrog introduced the **JFrog Software Supply Chain Traffic Controller**, described as “one trusted path for every software package.” It was announced together with integrations with **Zscaler, Cloudflare, and Netskope**, enabling organizations to control open-source consumption at the network edge.

   The Traffic Controller:
   - Stops malicious packages at the network level before they reach users’ machines.
   - Automatically reroutes software-package download requests through **JFrog Artifactory** as the single source of truth.
   - Works with SASE solutions and **JFrog Curation**.
   - Applies to software packages and artifacts used by developers, AI agents, and non-engineering employees.
   - Provides network-layer enforcement intended to prevent bypasses.
   - Transparently reroutes outbound package downloads rather than simply blocking out-of-policy requests.
   - Causes JFrog Curation to inspect packages against configured **security, license, and quality policies** before they enter the organization.
   - Delivers compliant packages without interruption.
   - Stops malicious packages and, when available, automatically serves a safe approved version.
   - Creates a complete, auditable record of packages entering the organization.

   **Availability:** The release states that **“The JFrog Traffic Controller solution is available immediately through JFrog Curation.”**

   **Initial gateway security solutions supported:**

   | Solution | Function described in the release |
   |---|---|
   | **Zscaler Internet Access™ (ZIA™)** | Identifies and curates the supply chain software package traffic through JFrog. |
   | **Cloudflare Gateway** | Can be configured to TLS-inspect public registry traffic and apply firewall policies to redirect package requests to JFrog Artifactory. |
   | **Netskope One SSE** | Applies real-time protection policies to redirect package manager traffic through JFrog, with browser passthrough to preserve the developer experience. |

   **Material product/commercial significance stated on the page:**
   - Traffic Controller extends JFrog’s protection to the **network edge**, beyond pipeline-level controls.
   - Artifactory is positioned as the software supply chain’s system of record for storing, managing, and governing binaries and packages.
   - Combined with JFrog Curation, the platform is positioned as a single source of truth protected by policy-driven controls against malicious, risky, or unwanted packages.
   - The product is designed as a **universal enforcement layer** that integrates with leading SASE providers while allowing customers to choose their preferred SASE solution.
   - The release specifically targets governance gaps involving AI coding agents, autonomous build tools, and non-engineering employees that may download dependencies directly from public registries.
   - JFrog stated that support for additional SASE partners is expected to follow.
   - The release does not provide pricing, revenue guidance, bookings, customer-count impact, or other quantified commercial terms for Traffic Controller.

   **Context cited in the release:**
   - JFrog’s 2026 Software Supply Chain Security State of the Union reported a **451% year-over-year surge in malicious packages**, reaching **over 171,000 unique instances**.
   - **40%** of organizations reportedly have malicious-package detection capabilities.
   - Secrets detection is reportedly active in **28% of enterprises**.

   **Customer example:** Adyen uses JFrog Curation as a real-time firewall to block malicious open-source packages from entering its software pipelines. Adyen’s stated objective is to enable development without disrupting developers’ workflows.
